**Finding: deviation (LICENSE — Licence grant scope)**

- **Where:** Section 1.4 (p0008–p0009), read with the assignment clause (p0063).
- **What the document has:** The only grant in our favour is HDI's obligation to provide "access to, and the right to use" the hosting system plus HDI's software and Content administration tools. The one express licence elsewhere (p0038) runs *from* us to HDI over the Deerskin Marks, so it is out of scope and not flagged.
- **Why it fails the fallback:** The Section 1.4 rights name only "the Company" — no affiliates, no contractors operating the Site on our behalf, no irrevocability during the term, and no successor transfer. Section 10.3 compounds this: it benefits successors and assigns but then states "no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement", removing any path to add affiliates or contractors. That misses the fallback (affiliates on written notice) on a material term.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** A single inserted paragraph 1.4.1 extending the Section 1.4 access/use rights to our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, confirming they are irrevocable during the term (subject only to Section 4 termination), and making them transferable to a successor by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets — with affiliate coverage on written notice offered as a fallback in the comment.
